# RealityRouter for LLMs and AI Agents

RealityRouter is a self-hosted, OpenAI-compatible LLM router. For each request it
scores every model in the user's pool on expected utility — probability of
success, cost, latency — and routes to the cheapest model likely to succeed. The
user brings their own provider keys; nothing is proxied through a third party.

This file is the short, operational version. Full docs:
https://realityrouter.dev/llms-full.txt

## First: find the endpoint, never assume it

```bash
reality-router status --json
```

Parse `base_url` (for example `http://localhost:8000/v1`) and `dashboard_url`.
**Do not hardcode port 8000** — the router moves when the port is taken.
`status` reports `"status": "running"` for a router started any way, including
Docker or systemd, with `managed_by` saying which.

## Endpoints

| Path | Protocol | Used by |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `/v1/chat/completions` | OpenAI Chat Completions | most clients |
| `/v1/responses` | OpenAI Responses API | Codex CLI, OpenClaw |
| `/v1/messages` | Anthropic Messages | Claude Code |
| `/v1/models` | model list | discovery |
| `/metrics/dashboard` | HTML dashboard | humans |
| `/health` | liveness, never requires a key | monitoring |

Send `"model": "auto"` to let the router choose. Any id from `/v1/models` pins
one instead.

## Authentication

By default the router accepts any request, so any placeholder key (`rr-local`)
works. If `ROUTER_API_KEYS` is set in `~/.reality_router/.env` (comma-separated),
every path except `/`, `/health` and the agent card requires one of those keys,
sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, as `x-api-key: <key>` (Anthropic clients),
or as HTTP Basic with the key as the password (the dashboard, in a browser).

To find out which applies: `curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' <base_url>/models`
— 401 means a key is required.

Turn keys on **before** the router is reachable from anywhere you do not control.
An unauthenticated router at a public address is an open proxy to the operator's
provider credits. `reality-router expose` puts the router behind a public HTTPS
tunnel and refuses to run unless a key is being enforced — it is how Cursor is
supported, because Cursor's requests come from Cursor's cloud and can never reach
`localhost`.

## CLI, headless

Every command below is safe without a TTY. `--json` means a machine is calling
and no command will prompt.

```bash
reality-router setup --agent            # zero-prompt setup, auto-detects keys
reality-router setup --non-interactive  # strict: fails if anything is missing
reality-router auth --agent --json      # SSO device flow, NDJSON events
reality-router status --json            # endpoint, port, pid, model counts
reality-router doctor --json            # active diagnostics, see exit codes
reality-router stop --json              # stop a CLI-started router
reality-router expose                   # public HTTPS address + API key
reality-router models --json
reality-router models --disable-model <id> --json
reality-router models --enable-model <id> --json
reality-router --set KEY=VALUE --json   # write config without hand-editing .env
```

`doctor` exit codes: `0` healthy, `10` no config file, `11` no SSO token,
`12` no provider credentials, `13` Ollama configured, unreachable, and no other
provider, `14` port taken by something that is not RealityRouter. A healthy
router occupying its own port is not an error, and a missing Ollama alongside
working cloud providers is reported under `warnings`, not `issues`.

## Installation

```bash
# Linux/macOS (idempotent, installs a wrapper to ~/.local/bin)
curl -fsSL https://github.com/Lars-confi/RealityRouter/raw/main/install.sh | bash

# Windows PowerShell
irm https://github.com/Lars-confi/RealityRouter/raw/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

Two agent skills cover install and tool wiring end to end, including which
questions to ask the user: `skills/install-realityrouter` and
`skills/connect-tool-to-realityrouter`. See `docs/agent-install.md`.

## Connecting a client

Point the tool at `base_url` and set its model to `auto`. Per-tool specifics,
including the traps, are in `docs/integrations.md`:

- **Claude Code** — `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` **without** `/v1`; it appends
  `/v1/messages` itself
- **Codex CLI** — Responses API only; leave `wire_api` unset
- **VS Code** — built-in chat, Custom Endpoint, no Copilot plan needed
- **Cursor** — needs a public address and a key (see above)
- **Aider** — add `X-Agent-ID` via `.aider.model.settings.yml` to be named in the
  dashboard; it identifies itself as `OpenAI/Python` otherwise
- **Zed, Cline, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes, Roo Code** — OpenAI-compatible
  provider blocks

## Environment & secrets

Precedence: `CLI flags > environment variables > .env > auto-detect > fallbacks`.
Config lives in `~/.reality_router/.env` (mode 600). Never print API keys, SSO
tokens or router keys into output, logs or a shared transcript. Ask the user for
provider keys rather than reading them out of other tools' configuration.
